paragraphs: Abba Shaul of Beit Marmesha. He was unique in his generation and like a pupil-colleague of Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai. ‘Abba Shaul says in his name’: Avot chapter 2, but there it is simply Abba Shaul, not ‘of Beit Remesha.’ Rav Tzemah Gaon, however, explains ‘in his name’ as ‘in his own name.’ In Semahot chapter 12 he instructed his sons to bury him at his father’s feet and remove the tekhelet from his cloak. The checked Semahot names Abba Shaul ben Ketanim. See Tosafot, Bava Batra 74a: Abba Shaul ben Botnit gave this instruction. At present I do not have Semahot before me. He used to bury the dead, etc., Ha-Mappelet (Yuhasin, chronological section). Thus it appears that the Abba Shaul mentioned just before this was the one from Beit Marmesha; I do not know whence he derived this.
